The first computer processors were made from vacuum tubes. These were large, hot, unreliable devices that consumed a lot of power. They were replaced by transistors, which were smaller, cooler and more reliable. Transistors were the basis of the integrated circuit, which allowed thousands of transistors to be placed on a single chip.

Chapter 2: The rise of the microprocessor

The first microprocessor, the Intel 4004, was released in 1971. It was a 4-bit processor that could perform basic arithmetic operations. The 8080, released in 1974, was a 8-bit processor
